title: Communication in Organisations
summary: 管理者通过沟通 coordinate、direct、influence、learn；有效沟通 = 信息 + 足够的共同理解（shared meaning）→ 适当行动
发送 ≠ 收到 ≠ 理解 ≠ 同意；共同理解不要求所有人想法相同
Shannon–Weaver (1949)：source → transmitter → channel → receiver → destination，noise 干扰；是线性传输模型，不能单独解释互动反馈
Encoding（发送者把想法变消息）vs Decoding（接收者依背景解释）；噪声分 Physical、Semantic、Psychological、Organisational 四类
反馈：让对方用自己的话说出任务、标准、期限，「懂了吗」不够；Sensemaking (Weick, 1995)：cue → interpret → act → update
7%/38%/55% (Mehrabian) 不能当所有沟通的通用比例，只适用于态度/情感线索与不一致消息
方向：Downward（过载、失真）、Upward（恐惧、过滤、沉默）、Horizontal（部门孤岛）；正式 ≠ 向下，非正式 ≠ 谣言
网络：Chain、Wheel、All-channel；集中式适合简单任务，分散式适合复杂任务（Bavelas 1950, Leavitt 1951），结构要 fit the task
Media Richness Theory (Daft & Lengel)：快速反馈、多种线索、个人化、自然语言；越模糊越需要丰富渠道；richness ≠ 字数或技术新旧
Channel Expansion Theory (Carlson & Zmud, 1999)：对渠道、主题、组织、沟通伙伴的经验使同一媒介感觉更丰富
社交媒体可供性 (Treem & Leonardi, 2013)：Visibility、Persistence、Editability、Association；affordance 是可能性，不是必然结果
高/低语境 (Hall, 1976) 是框架不是国籍标签；Age / Period / Cohort 效应难分离；Ravid 等 (2025) 元分析：系统且有意义的世代差异很少
失败环节：编码、注意、解释、行动；障碍：知觉选择、模糊与术语、过载 (Marlow 2018)、过滤与 MUM 效应 (Rosen & Tesser 1970)、员工沉默
Voice 两问：Is it safe to speak up? Will it make a difference?（Morrison）；Kluger (2024) 倾听 r = .39（相关不是 39%）；Edmondson (1999) 51 个团队，心理安全与学习行为相关

concepts.def: Receivers understand enough of the intended meaning to take appropriate action.
concepts.defZh: 信息 → 解释 → 共同理解 → 行动；经理要检查后两步。
concepts.one: 接收者理解了足够的本意并能据此正确行动，而不只是收到了消息。
concepts.eg: 经理说「今天优先处理投诉」，员工却理解成暂停所有销售，消息到了但共同理解没形成。
concepts.like: 像传球不只要把球传到对方脚下，还要他知道该往哪儿踢。

concepts.def: A classic linear model: information source, transmitter, channel, receiver and destination, with noise interfering in transmission.
concepts.defZh: 最初关注信号传输，不能单独解释职场互动反馈和意义协商。
concepts.one: 经典线性模型：信息从信源经发射器和渠道传到接收端，途中可能被噪声干扰。
concepts.eg: 电台播报天气时，电流杂音盖住了「暴雨」两个字，收音机这头就漏掉了关键内容。
concepts.like: 像单向的传送带，只管把货送到，不管对方看不看得懂。

concepts.def: Encoding is the sender turning ideas into words, symbols or behaviour; decoding is the receiver interpreting the message based on their background.
concepts.defZh: 错误可能发生在任一端。
concepts.one: 发送者把想法变成话语或符号叫编码，接收者按自己的背景去理解叫解码。
concepts.eg: 主管说「把报告写得更战略一点」，新员工理解成多加行业背景，两人朝不同方向做。
concepts.like: 像出谜语和猜谜语，谜面怎么写、怎么猜，两头都可能出错。

concepts.def: Anything that interferes with transmitting or understanding a message: physical, semantic, psychological or organisational.
concepts.defZh: 物理（声音、技术故障）、语义（术语、模糊词）、心理（压力、预设）、组织（层级、部门隔阂、过载）。
concepts.one: 任何干扰信息传递或理解的东西，分物理、语义、心理和组织四类。
concepts.eg: 「周五完成」在网络不好的会议里听不清，各部门标准又不一样，这些都是噪声。
concepts.like: 像打电话时的杂音、听不懂的方言和坏心情，都会让话听不明白。

concepts.def: People form plausible interpretations from cues, act on them, and update their understanding with new information.
concepts.defZh: Weick (1995)；同一公告可被理解成机会、威胁或已定结论。
concepts.one: 人们根据手头的线索形成一个说得通的解释并行动，再用新信息不断修正。
concepts.eg: 公司宣布要「更敏捷」，有人想到试新方法，有人担心裁员，经理补充说明后大家才更新理解。
concepts.like: 像在雾中开车，先凭看到的路标判断方向，越开越清楚再调整。

concepts.zh: 向下 / 向上 / 横向沟通
concepts.def: Downward: goals and instructions to lower levels; upward: progress, problems and bad news to management; horizontal: coordination among peers and functions.
concepts.defZh: 风险分别是过载失真、过滤沉默、部门孤岛。
concepts.one: 向下是传目标和指令，向上是报进度和坏消息，横向是同级和部门之间协调。
concepts.eg: 店长布置先处理退货是向下，员工报告排班漏洞是向上，营销部找运营部确认库存是横向。
concepts.like: 像大楼的电梯和走廊：上下楼传指令和问题，走廊连通隔壁。

concepts.def: Formal communication is deliberately designed by the organisation; informal communication emerges from relationships and daily interaction.
concepts.defZh: 正式不等于只能向下，非正式不等于全是谣言。
concepts.one: 正式沟通由组织有意设计，非正式沟通从人际关系和日常互动中自然形成。
concepts.eg: 公司用官方邮件公布办公室调整，同事午休时聊各自的理解，这些闲聊会影响大家怎么看那封邮件。
concepts.like: 像学校的正式课表和课间走廊里的闲聊，两条线都在传信息。

concepts.zh: 链式 / 轮式 / 全通道网络
concepts.def: Chain links people in sequence; wheel routes information through one central member; all-channel gives members many direct connections.
concepts.defZh: 轮式快速集中但中心可能过载；全通道适合复杂、创造性、相互依赖工作。
concepts.one: 链式按顺序一个传一个，轮式都经过一个中心，全通道是成员彼此直接相连。
concepts.eg: 项目组所有问题都先交给协调员再转告别人，这是轮式；协调员忙不过来，信息就堵在中心。
concepts.like: 像传话游戏、自行车轮的辐条和圆桌讨论这三种连法。

concepts.def: Channels differ in their capacity to reduce ambiguity, based on rapid feedback, multiple cues, personalisation and natural language.
concepts.defZh: Daft & Lengel；连续线：报告 → 邮件 → 聊天 → 电话 → 视频 → 面对面，但不是绝对排名。
concepts.one: 渠道减少歧义的能力不同，信息越模糊，越需要反馈快、线索多的丰富渠道。
concepts.eg: 员工把重组公告理解成要被裁了，经理安排视频问答当面澄清，而不是再转发一遍文字。
concepts.like: 像解释一场复杂的误会，当面聊比发短信更容易说清楚。

concepts.def: Perceived richness depends on experience with the channel, topic, organisational context and communication partner.
concepts.defZh: Carlson & Zmud (1999)；不是增加软件功能。
concepts.one: 一个渠道感觉有多丰富，还取决于你对这个渠道、话题、组织和对方有多熟。
concepts.eg: 同一个项目群里，老成员看到一句缩写就能动手，新成员却需要别人额外解释。
concepts.like: 像老朋友之间发一个表情包就懂，陌生人却得说一大段。

concepts.def: Visibility, persistence, editability and association: action possibilities that technology enables.
concepts.defZh: Treem & Leonardi (2013)；可能也被用于印象管理或监视。
concepts.one: 可见、持久、可编辑、可关联四种特性，让信息更容易被看见、留存和连接。
concepts.eg: 公司知识平台公开技术讨论、保留旧答案、可以修改还能找到贡献者，新人顺着线索就能求助。
concepts.like: 像公共留言墙：人人能看、一直留着、能补充，还找得到作者。

concepts.zh: 高语境 / 低语境沟通
concepts.def: High-context relies more on relationships, shared background and nonverbal cues; low-context states meaning more explicitly in words.
concepts.defZh: Hall (1976)；Kittler 等 (2011) 指出国家排名缺乏严格经验支持。
concepts.one: 高语境靠关系、共同背景和非言语线索传意，低语境把意思直接写在字面上。
concepts.eg: 经理说「报告还有提升空间」可能被当成随口建议，补一句「周五三点前改好第二节」就清楚了。
concepts.like: 像老夫妻一个眼神就懂，和新同事则得把话说全。

concepts.zh: 年龄 / 时期 / 出生群体效应
concepts.def: Age effects come from life or career stage; period effects from events affecting many people at once; cohort effects from a birth group's historical background.
concepts.defZh: 三者交织难以分离；Rudolph 等 (2021)。
concepts.one: 年龄效应看人生阶段，时期效应看大家同时经历的事，群体效应看出生年代。
concepts.eg: 疫情后各个年龄层都开始用视频开会，这主要是时期效应，不能说成是 Gen Z 的特征。
concepts.like: 像猜人为何穿厚外套：年纪大、今天冷，还是那代人的习惯？

concepts.def: Too many, repeated or low-value messages and meetings scatter attention and hide priorities.
concepts.defZh: Marlow 等 (2018)；质量比数量更重要。
concepts.one: 消息和会议太多太杂，注意力被打散，真正重要的事反而被淹没。
concepts.eg: 主管在邮件、群聊和会议里发了十几条提醒，员工反而漏掉了唯一紧急的截止日期。
concepts.like: 像一屋子闹钟同时响，反而找不到真正叫你起床的那一个。

concepts.def: Selecting, softening or changing information passed upward.
concepts.defZh: 和知觉选择不同：过滤改变传给别人的内容。
concepts.one: 往上传话时有选择地删减、弱化或改写内容，上级听到的版本就变了样。
concepts.eg: 员工说「期限做不到」，中层转成「可能稍有延误」，高层听到的是「基本按计划推进」。
concepts.like: 像坏消息一层层加糖，传到最上面已经尝不出原味了。

concepts.def: Reluctance to transmit unpleasant news.
concepts.defZh: Rosen & Tesser (1970)。
concepts.one: 人们不愿意传递让人不舒服的消息，所以坏消息常常被拖着或憋着不说。
concepts.eg: 团队早就知道客户的期限做不到却不上报，拖到截止前两天才告诉客户会延误。
concepts.like: 像孩子考砸了，迟迟不敢把试卷拿给父母签字。

concepts.def: Voice is proactively raising ideas or concerns to improve work; silence is withholding useful information.
concepts.defZh: Morrison (2014, 2023)；沉默不等于赞同。
concepts.one: 发声是主动提意见或担忧，沉默是明知有用信息却不说，但不等于同意。
concepts.eg: 员工发现流程会让客户重复付款，但怕被责怪、觉得说了也没用，就选择不提。
concepts.like: 像乘客发现车门没关好，喊不喊得看司机会不会骂人。

concepts.def: A climate where relevant information reaches those who need it, built through accessibility, candour and responsiveness.
concepts.defZh: 不是公开每场谈话。
concepts.one: 让相关信息能到达需要它的人，靠容易接近、坦诚和认真回应来建立。
concepts.eg: 主管说「随时来找我」却每次都打断坏消息，没人敢说；认真听完风险并跟进，门才真的开着。
concepts.like: 像一扇门不只要开着，进去的人还不能被骂出来。

concepts.def: Attending carefully, clarifying and paraphrasing to confirm meaning, then responding so the other person feels understood.
concepts.defZh: 先注意，再澄清复述，最后回应；不急着评价。
concepts.one: 专心听，用提问和复述确认自己理解对了，再回应，让对方觉得被理解。
concepts.eg: 员工抱怨预算要求，经理先复述一遍：「你担心的是数据没法验证，不是目标太高，对吗？」
concepts.like: 像服务员把你点的菜复述一遍，确认没听错再下单。

concepts.def: A shared belief that the team is safe for interpersonal risk-taking such as asking questions, admitting mistakes or disagreeing.
concepts.defZh: Edmondson (1999)，51 个团队；不等于永远同意或无需承担责任。
concepts.one: 团队成员共同相信，在这里提问、认错、提出不同意见都不会被羞辱或惩罚。
concepts.eg: 飞行员发现仪表异常能马上说出来而不怕被羞辱，团队就更可能及时学习和纠错。
concepts.like: 像一个允许答错的课堂，大家才敢举手。

tf.q: If a message has been sent and received, effective communication has occurred.
tf.exp: 发出、收到、理解、同意是四件不同的事，有效沟通要形成共同理解并带来合适的行动。

tf.q: The Shannon–Weaver model is a linear transmission model that cannot by itself explain interactive feedback and negotiation of meaning at work.
tf.exp: 它是一个线性的传输模型，最初关心的是信号怎么传，所以解释不了职场里的互动和反馈。

tf.q: According to the lecture, the 7%/38%/55% rule shows that 93% of all communication is nonverbal.
tf.exp: 那个实验只涉及态度和情感线索，以及不一致的消息，不能推广成所有沟通的比例。

tf.q: Formal communication can carry upward and horizontal information, not only downward instructions.
tf.exp: 正式沟通不等于只能向下传指令，正式渠道同样可以向上报告和横向协调。

tf.q: Classic network studies (Bavelas, Leavitt) suggest centralised networks handle simple problems efficiently, while decentralised networks suit complex problems better.
tf.exp: 集中式网络处理简单任务效率高，分散式更适合复杂任务，关键是结构要和任务匹配。

tf.q: Media richness refers to the length of a message or the newness of the technology used.
tf.exp: 丰富度看的是渠道减少歧义的能力，比如反馈快不快、线索多不多，和字数、技术新旧无关。

tf.q: Channel Expansion Theory suggests that the same chat tool can feel richer to experienced team members than to newcomers.
tf.exp: 对渠道、话题、组织和对方越熟悉，同一个工具就感觉越丰富，老成员自然比新人觉得更好用。

tf.q: Social media affordances guarantee that knowledge sharing will improve once a platform is installed.
tf.exp: 可供性只是提供了行动的可能，不保证结果；如果大家怕公开提问或频道被淹没，收益就会下降。

tf.q: High-context and low-context communication should not be used to predict each individual's style from their nationality.
tf.exp: 高低语境是帮你留意差异的框架，不是固定的国籍标签，不能拿来预测某个人的风格。

tf.q: Ravid, Costanza and Romero's (2025) meta-analysis directly proved that generations have no differences in communication preferences.
tf.exp: 这项元分析看的是工作态度和价值观，没有直接检验沟通偏好，也不等于说所有人都一样。

tf.q: Employee silence means employees agree with management's decisions.
tf.exp: 沉默是把有用的信息憋着不说，不等于赞同，可能是怕说了挨骂或觉得说了也没用。

tf.q: Kluger et al.'s (2024) correlation of r = .39 between perceived listening and work outcomes means listening improves outcomes by 39%.
tf.exp: 这里的 .39 是相关系数，不是提升的百分比，相关也证明不了因果。

tf.q: Edmondson's (1999) study of 51 work teams found that psychological safety was associated with team learning behaviour.
tf.exp: 研究报告的是心理安全和团队学习行为之间的关联，不能把它改写成普遍的因果定律。

tf.q: In crisis communication, honestly separating verified facts from unknowns supports credibility more than false certainty.
tf.exp: 坦诚分开已核实的事实和未知，比假装确定更可信；还要及时、一致、关心受影响者并持续更新。

tf.q: Closing the feedback loop on employee voice means managers must implement every suggestion.
tf.exp: 闭环是指对员工的意见给出回应，没采纳也要解释原因，不是承诺每条建议都照做。

mcq.q: A supervisor tells a new analyst to make a report 'more strategic', meaning 'show the client our recommendations'. The analyst adds more industry background instead. Where did the breakdown most clearly occur?
options: A mismatch between encoding and decoding
mcq.exp: 主管编码时想的是「给客户看建议」，分析师解码成「补行业背景」，两头对不上，问题出在编码和解码不匹配。

mcq.q: During a restructuring, an anxious employee reads a neutral announcement as a threat to her job. Which type of noise is this?
mcq.exp: 压力、情绪和预设立场让人把中性消息读歪，这属于心理噪声；语义噪声指的是词义和术语不清。

mcq.q: Different departments interpret 'complete by Friday' differently because they use different standards for 'complete'. Which response best targets this noise?
options: Clarify the meaning of terms, standards and deadlines
mcq.exp: 各部门对「完成」的标准不同，是语义噪声，所以要把词义、标准和期限讲清楚；修网络只能解决物理噪声。

mcq.q: A manager wants to check whether an employee has understood a task. Which approach is most effective according to the lecture?
options: Ask the employee what they will do first, what they will deliver and by when
mcq.exp: 让员工用自己的话说出先做什么、交付什么、什么时候交，才看得出他是否真懂；问一句「懂了吗」大多只会得到「懂了」。

mcq.q: A company announces it will become 'more agile'. Some staff see opportunity, others fear layoffs. The manager then explains what is decided, what is not, and next steps. Which concept explains the staff's varied responses?
mcq.exp: 员工各自根据线索形成说得通的解释，经理补充信息后大家再更新理解，这是意义建构（sensemaking）。

mcq.q: In a project team, all questions must go to one coordinator who passes information to others. When the coordinator is overloaded, information stalls. Which network is this?
mcq.exp: 所有信息都要经过协调员这一个中心，这是轮式网络；它的主要弱点就是中心一忙，信息就堵住。

mcq.q: A team designing new packaging needs design, sales and production to integrate different knowledge. Which network best fits this task?
mcq.exp: 要整合三个部门的不同知识，属于复杂、相互依赖的工作，成员之间直接相连的全通道网络最合适。

mcq.q: A manager must deliver sensitive performance feedback. Which approach best fits the lecture's guidance?
options: An email only, to keep a record
A text message to save time
A private face-to-face or video conversation followed by a short written summary
mcq.exp: 敏感的反馈需要能当场互动、又能保密的丰富渠道，所以先面谈或视频，再用书面总结留个记录；只发邮件或短信太单薄。

mcq.q: A manager needs to find someone among 200 colleagues with specific technical expertise. Which affordances make an internal knowledge platform suitable?
mcq.exp: 可见性帮你看到谁懂什么，持久性让旧讨论能被再利用，关联性把相关的人连起来，所以能找到专家。

mcq.q: Long-standing team members act on a one-word abbreviation in the project chat, while new members need explanations. Which theory explains this?
mcq.exp: 老成员对这个渠道、话题和同事更熟，同一条缩写对他们就「更丰富」，这是渠道扩展理论；媒介丰富度理论只看渠道本身。

mcq.q: After the pandemic, employees of all ages began using video meetings. A manager calls this a 'Gen Z trait'. What is the error?
options: It confuses a period effect with a cohort effect
It confuses an age effect with tenure
It is a correct cohort effect
It confuses horizontal with downward communication
mcq.exp: 疫情是所有年龄的人同时经历的事件，带来的变化是时期效应；把它说成 Gen Z 的特征，就是和群体效应搞混了。

mcq.q: An employee reports 'this deadline is impossible'; the middle manager says 'there may be a slight delay'; senior leaders hear 'broadly on track'. Which concepts best explain this?
mcq.exp: 坏消息每往上传一层就被弱化一次，这是过滤；大家不愿意当传坏消息的人，这是 MUM 效应。

mcq.q: A manager says 'my door is always open' but interrupts and criticises anyone who brings bad news. Which element of an open communication climate is most clearly missing?

Move the project to a chain network

mcq.q: Which statement about Media Richness Theory's channel continuum is most accurate?
options: Face-to-face is always better than written communication
It is a heuristic ordering; a well-designed written message can outperform a poorly run meeting
Richness depends on the size of attachments
Email is the richest channel because it keeps records

essay.q: Case: A project team believes a client deadline is unrealistic. The team leader instructs members to 'stay positive' and avoid escalating issues until they have a solution. Routine updates to senior managers report that the project is on track. Two days before the deadline, the client is told there will be a delay, damaging the relationship. Using concepts from this week, diagnose what went wrong and recommend how communication should be improved.
points: Identify blocked upward communication, filtering and the MUM effect
Explain employee silence using the two voice questions: safe to speak up? will it make a difference?
Explain that routine updates lacked feedback checks on deadline and risk
Recommend an open communication climate: accessibility, candour, responsiveness; do not punish messengers
Recommend specific practices: risk-focused updates, interactive risk discussion plus written record, closing the loop
Suggest how to verify improvement, e.g. leaders restating risks and decisions needed
essay.model: The core problem was blocked upward communication. The real risk never entered routine updates, so senior managers made judgements based on incomplete information. Two mechanisms explain this. First, filtering and the MUM effect: people are reluctant to transmit unpleasant news, and each layer softened the message until 'impossible' became 'on track'. Second, employee silence: the instruction to 'stay positive' and to escalate only with a solution raised the cost of speaking up. Using Morrison's two questions, staff likely felt it was neither safe nor useful to raise concerns. Routine updates also reported surface progress without any feedback check on deadline risk. To fix this, the manager should immediately verify the risk and tell the client and leaders what is known and what is uncertain. Updates should explicitly list deadline gaps, risks, impacts and decisions required. Because risk is ambiguous, a rich, interactive discussion where leaders can ask questions should be held, followed by a written record. Leaders should build an open climate through accessibility, candour and responsiveness: invite concerns before asking for agreement, respond constructively to bad news, never punish the messenger, and close the loop by reporting owners, actions and the next update time. Improvement can be checked by asking senior managers to restate current risks and by rewarding accurate, timely risk reports rather than good news alone.

essay.q: Case: A multinational firm is announcing a major restructuring to 600 employees across three countries. The HR director plans to send one long email full of internal acronyms on a Friday evening. A manager also suggests putting older staff on email-only updates and younger staff on chat-only updates because 'that is what each generation prefers'. Evaluate the plan using this week's concepts and propose a better communication approach.
points: Apply Media Richness Theory: an ambiguous, sensitive message needs richer, interactive channels
Identify semantic noise from acronyms and psychological noise from anxiety; sensemaking risks
Recommend combining channels: written statement for reach and persistence plus interactive Q&A
Apply cross-cultural guidance: clarify expectations, check meaning, avoid idioms and acronyms; do not stereotype by nationality
Critique generational stereotyping using age/period/cohort and Ravid et al. (2025); ask individual preferences
Include feedback checks and ongoing updates
essay.model: A major restructuring is ambiguous and sensitive, so a single long email is a poor fit. Media Richness Theory suggests that ambiguous messages need channels with rapid feedback, multiple cues and personalisation. Employees will engage in sensemaking: some may interpret the change as a threat, and anxiety creates psychological noise, while internal acronyms add semantic noise, especially across countries. A Friday-evening email also leaves people to fill the gaps over the weekend. A better approach combines channels. A clear written statement provides reach and a persistent reference, followed by interactive meetings or video Q&A where managers explain what is decided, what is not yet known and the next steps. Managers should check understanding by inviting employees to describe what the change means for their own roles. Across cultures, managers should state key expectations clearly, avoid idioms, jokes and acronyms, and remain curious rather than assuming any individual's style from high- or low-context national labels. The generational plan is stereotyping. Differences in channel use may reflect age, period or cohort effects, which are hard to separate, and Ravid et al.'s (2025) meta-analysis found few systematic and meaningful generational differences in work outcomes. Managers should instead ask individuals about their preferences and agree on consistent confirmation rules for urgent messages. Ongoing updates should follow.

essay.q: Case: A hospital unit has a suggestion box and an 'open door' policy, yet junior nurses rarely report near-miss medication errors. When one nurse raised a concern last year, the senior nurse said she should 'stop complaining' and nothing changed. Using concepts from this week, explain why reporting is low and what the unit manager should do.
points: Explain voice versus silence and that silence does not mean agreement
Apply the two voice questions: safety and efficacy
Explain team psychological safety (Edmondson, 1999) and its limits (association, not universal causation)
Note a suggestion box only provides an entry point, not safety or responsiveness
Recommend managerial practices: invite concerns, respond constructively, do not punish the messenger, separate issue from person, follow up
Recommend active listening and appropriate question types
essay.model: The low reporting reflects employee silence: nurses are withholding useful information about near-misses. Silence is not agreement and not simply being quiet. According to Morrison, employees ask whether it is safe to speak up and whether speaking up will make a difference. Here both answers appear to be no: the earlier concern was dismissed as complaining, and nothing changed. A suggestion box and an 'open door' only provide an entry point; they cannot create safety or responsiveness on their own. The unit lacks team psychological safety, the shared belief that asking questions, admitting mistakes and raising problems are safe. Edmondson's (1999) study of 51 teams found psychological safety was associated with team learning behaviour, although this is a correlation rather than a universal law. Psychological safety does not mean removing accountability; it means making it safe to raise risks. The manager should actively invite concerns before asking for agreement, respond constructively to bad news, separate the issue from the person, never punish the messenger, and admit uncertainty or mistakes. Using active listening and open, clarifying and reflective questions, the manager can understand each report. Crucially, the manager should close the loop by explaining what was changed or why not. Over time this shows staff that speaking up is both safe and useful.
